name: background
description: Foundations contract for the background-treatment system: the bg--{color}[--pattern--{type}] class grammar, its foreground-color cascade, border-color overrides under backgrounds, and the pattern-image layer. UIDS owns the grammar and the color/pattern tokens; uids_base (SiteNow) is the downstream consumer whose Layout Builder background options select these classes. Not a component — no Vue file. It DOES own one Figma component set as of 2026-08-24 (`Backgrounds`, 170:55): a documentation surface for the class grammar, not an instanceable component. See changes[2].

figma.note: The governed surface is the component set `Backgrounds` (170:55, 16 variants, 800×300). All 11 tokensUsed entries are bound on it — solid fill, text, link, border — verified live 2026-08-24. The 16 doc frames (163:5 … 163:61) are SUPERSEDED but still present, pending deletion by hand: see changes[2](f). The pattern layer is an IMAGE paint and a Figma variable is COLOR/FLOAT/STRING/BOOLEAN, so no pattern can ever be bound or verified by any checker — it is governed by instruction only, via the set description and rules.json's backgrounds-by-class.

options.name: color
options.description: Background color of the wrapping element. No default: the absence of any bg--{color} class IS the page-default background (semantic color/background), not a member of this enum. Combines with `pattern` into the single frozen class bg--{color}[--pattern--{type}] — see identity.description and knownIssues for why the grammar itself is the versioned shape.

code.notes: shared/background.ts exposes two prop shapes over this grammar: props.background (colors array ['', 'black', 'gold', 'gray', 'white'], addBackgroundClass prefixes 'bg--') for color-only consumers, and allBackgroundProps.background (allBackgroundOptions, 16 literal combo strings like 'gold--pattern--particle') for consumers that also expose pattern. Neither prop shape composes color+pattern independently at the JS layer — the combined string IS the value; there is no code path that ORs a separate color prop with a separate pattern prop.

options.name: pattern
options.description: Background image pattern layered over `color`. 'none' omits the --pattern--{type} suffix entirely (bg--{color} alone). 'community' and 'particle' are color-tinted PNG photographic textures; 'brain' is a solid-color SVG line pattern. See geometryNotTokenized for the fixed background-size per pattern and knownIssues for the full asset-per-combo map (some combos share an image file).

code.notes: Values above are the SUFFIX fragment appended to the color class (bg--{color}--pattern--{type}), not a standalone selector — 'none' adds no suffix. See the `color` option's code.notes for how shared/background.ts actually exposes the two axes as one combined prop string.

geometryNotTokenized.pattern-image-assets: 12 url() references, 11 distinct files (community-pattern--gray.png is shared, see knownIssues), in _background-mixins.scss's $backgrounds map ($imgpath = '../../assets/images', _variables.scss:26). BLACK AND GOLD, $backgrounds lines: bg--black--pattern--brain -> brain-pattern-black.svg (L10); --community -> community-pattern--black.png (L15); --particle -> particle-pattern--black.png (L20); bg--gold--pattern--brain -> brain-pattern-reversed.svg (L30); --community -> community-pattern--white.png (L35); --particle -> particle-pattern.png (L40). Gray and white: pattern-image-assets-gray-white.
geometryNotTokenized.pattern-background-size: Fixed, not a scale: [class*="--pattern--particle"] = 1400px (_background.scss:16-19); [class*="--pattern--community"] = 1000px (_background.scss:21-24); brain gets no override so it renders at the default background-size: auto auto set for any bg+pattern combo (_background.scss:11-14).
geometryNotTokenized.pattern-background-position: center center, set for any [class*="bg--"][class*="--pattern--"] combination alongside the default auto auto sizing (_background.scss:11-14).
geometryNotTokenized.pattern-opacity: MEASURED 2026-08-22 — this is the only place these levels are written down, in any of the five views. There is NO CSS opacity anywhere in the pattern system: _background-mixins.scss:120-140 emits only background-color + background-image, _background.scss:11-24 only size and position, and a live DOM check of all 12 swatches reads opacity:1, filter:none, mix-blend-mode:normal, background-blend-mode:normal and content:none on both pseudo-elements. Strength is ENTIRELY baked into the asset, two different ways: pattern-opacity-brain and pattern-opacity-pngs. Method: pattern-opacity-method.
geometryNotTokenized.pattern-image-assets-gray-white: Continues pattern-image-assets — GRAY AND WHITE, with $backgrounds line numbers: bg--gray--pattern--brain -> brain-pattern-white.svg (L50); --community -> community-pattern--gray.png (L55); --particle -> particle-pattern--white.png (L60); bg--white--pattern--brain -> brain-pattern.svg (L70); --community -> community-pattern--gray.png (L75, same file as gray's); --particle -> particle-pattern--gold.png (L80). Asset paths are not part of the token system; Figma swatches must be drawn from this exact map (see knownIssues).
geometryNotTokenized.pattern-opacity-brain: THE FOUR BRAIN SVGs declare strength as readable text at line 7 of each file: brain-pattern-black.svg .st0{opacity:0.15}, brain-pattern-reversed.svg 0.2, brain-pattern-white.svg 0.7, brain-pattern.svg 0.15 (brain-pattern-gray.svg declares none and is unused — not in $backgrounds). Those four are LEVELS, not distributions: exactly 5 alpha bins, ~84% zero and the rest at 25/50/75/100% of peak, i.e. line-art antialiasing.
geometryNotTokenized.pattern-opacity-pngs: THE SIX COMMUNITY/PARTICLE PNGs instead carry per-pixel alpha with 19-128 distinct values and 61-77% zero, so any single number for them is a PEAK and must be labelled one: black/community 0.212, black/particle 0.157, gold/community 0.400, gold/particle 0.271, gray/community 0.078 (black ink), gray/particle 0.898, white/community 0.078 (black ink), white/particle 0.271 (gold ink). Alpha alone never answers `how strong does this look` — gray/particle is 0.898 and yet composites to rgb(254,254,254), because it is white ink on #f3f3f3.
geometryNotTokenized.pattern-opacity-method: METHOD for pattern-opacity, so it can be re-run: draw the asset to a canvas at natural size, read alpha via getImageData, then re-composite against the swatch's computed background-color; the analytic bg x (1-a) + ink x a matched the browser's own source-over to ±0 on all 36 channels. The live DOM half was read off Storybook at :6007 — verify which checkout answers that port before trusting a repeat.

behavior: Each bg--{color}[--pattern--{type}] class sets background-color via color/bg/{color} — black and gold RIDE THE BRAND CHANNELS (4.x wrote variables.$secondary/$primary = var(--brand-secondary/-primary), so grayscale retheming must keep reaching section fills; a flat gold/black alias here would re-ship the Buttons bug), gray and white are flat — plus the type-mapped foreground cascade: type 'light' (gold/gray/white) applies color/on-light/text + color/on-light/link, type 'dark' (black) applies color/on-dark/text + color/on-dark/link, all through bg-fg-colors() (_background-mixins.scss:120-140; call site _background.scss:27). How that mixin dedups, and what silently breaks it: behavior[4].

[class*="bg--"] forces border-color: inherit onto all descendants and their ::before/::after (_background.scss:29-40), so nested elements never carry their own border color. The actual value is set on the wrapper itself by a second, separate rule set: gray/white/gold backgrounds plus the legacy .bg-pattern--brain / .bg-pattern--brain-reversed context classes resolve to color/border/default (_background.scss:43-49); black backgrounds plus .bg--black--pattern--brain / .bg-pattern--brain-black resolve to color/border/on-dark (_background.scss:51-55).

Nested-bg link-color exceptions: under a white or gray background, prose links (p, ul, ol, dl, cite, tbody, figcaption a, excluding .bttn) are restored to var(--link-color) even though the ancestor's inherited foreground color would otherwise apply (_background.scss:57-63). But gold or black backgrounds nested one level inside white/gray revert to inherit instead, i.e. they take the ancestor's on-light foreground rather than the restored link color (_background.scss:65-71).

Pattern backgrounds set a fixed, non-tokenized background-size: particle 1400px, community 1000px; brain takes no size override and renders at the default auto auto (_background.scss:11-24; see geometryNotTokenized).

THE FOREGROUND CASCADE ROUTES THROUGH A SASS PLACEHOLDER, and an SCSS swap can silently drop it. Every bg-fg-colors() call goes through placeholders.uids-dynamic-extend($bg-class) (_background-mixins.scss:96-100), which keys a Sass placeholder by the literal $bg-class string and only emits the declaration body the first time a given id is seen; a later call for the SAME id is a pure @extend, not a re-declaration. add-backgrounds() is called exactly once today, so this currently behaves as a 1:1 pass-through per class — but the $before/$after params exist so another selector context can request the same color's cascade again without duplicating it. Inlining the color/* rules directly per class instead of routing through bg-fg-colors() would silently drop that dedup path.
changes: 2026-08-22 — FIGMA'S PATTERN LEVELS ARE A DELIBERATE DESIGN CHANGE, NOT A FIDELITY BUG. SUPERSEDED 2026-08-24 by changes[2], which removed every level; read that first and do NOT restore them. the design system owner's ruling, taken after the measurement (changes[3]) not before it: keep the levels in component set 170:55 — black 0.30 across all three patterns; gold 0.50; gray brain 1.00, gray community 0.15, gray particle 1.00; white brain 0.15, community 0.30, particle 0.50 — even though they do not match production, because these swatches are read at thumbnail size, where production's true levels are close to invisible. THE MECHANISM STILL MATTERS: pattern strength is baked into the asset, so a Figma paint opacity MULTIPLIES that baked alpha rather than replacing it — 170:58 rendered a 0.239 peak from a 0.30 paint over an image carrying ~0.80 baked alpha, against production's 0.149.

2026-08-22 — WHAT changes[0]'s RULING DOES *NOT* COVER, left open deliberately. BOTH were closed 2026-08-24 by changes[2], the current state. (1) IMAGE IDENTITY: Figma backed 12 combos with only 7 distinct images. Hash 781dad9db9 served black, gold AND gray brain — three production files with three different inks and opacities — while the three doc frames labelled it brain-pattern-black.svg, brain-pattern-reversed.svg and brain-pattern-white.svg, so at most one label was true. 5af416b8a9 likewise served three particles, ab3577e809 two communities. The sharing was inverted where production genuinely shares a file: gray/community and white/community both use community-pattern--gray.png, yet Figma gave them two hashes at two opacities. Aspect ratios did not match the sources (brain 3168x2448 = 1.29 vs the 600x1201 SVG's 0.50). Wrong pictures are not a design choice. (2) is changes[4].

2026-08-24 — CONSOLIDATED ONTO ONE GOVERNED SURFACE. SUPERSEDES changes[0] and closes both defects changes[1] and changes[4] left open; read it before any of them. The design system owner's rulings; the consolidation plan lives in the research fork (.claude/plans/2026-08-24_backgrounds-consolidation-plan.md there). (a) THE FIGMA OPACITY LEVELS ARE GONE: every level changes[0] blessed is now paint opacity 1.00, because strength belongs in the asset exactly as production does it, and a dial in Figma teaches Make a mechanism the system does not have. Do NOT restore the levels. The rest of the consolidation: (b) changes[5], (c) changes[6], (d) and (e) changes[7], (f) changes[8].

2026-08-22, the measurement behind changes[0] — superseded with it by changes[2], kept because it is the only record of the gap. Rendered against production, mean pattern ink came out at black/brain 1.80x, black/community 1.30x, black/particle 1.56x, gold/brain 2.14x, gold/community 1.16x, gold/particle 1.54x, gray/brain 0.70x, gray/community 1.34x, gray/particle 0.85x, white/brain 1.08x, white/community 1.69x, white/particle 1.78x — scattered in BOTH directions with no common factor, so it could not be expressed as one multiplier and there was no arithmetic that turned it back into fidelity. Production's own levels, for comparison: a 0.149 peak on black/brain, means around 0.017-0.14.

2026-08-22, the second defect changes[1] left open — closed 2026-08-24 by changes[2]. (2) THE TWO FIGMA SURFACES DISAGREED WITH EACH OTHER: all 12 doc frames (163:8 … 163:61) carried image-paint opacity 1.00 while the set carried changes[0]'s levels, so a designer reading this file got two different answers to the same question — and at 1.00 over a ~0.80-alpha image, doc frame 163:8 rendered black/brain at roughly 5.3x production. Full evidence, method and error bars are in the research fork this work came from (.claude/plans/2026-08-22_backgrounds-measurement.md there); the numbers quoted here are the conclusion.

2026-08-24, changes[2] (b) — IMAGE IDENTITY FIXED. The 12 combos had been backed by 7 images with the sharing in the wrong places (changes[1]); they are now backed by 11 distinct images, the single shared pair being gray/community + white/community, which is the one pair production genuinely shares (community-pattern--gray.png). Every image was uploaded from the files named in geometryNotTokenized.pattern-image-assets, and the 12 resulting Figma hashes were read back and asserted against the upload responses.

2026-08-24, changes[2] (c) — BRAIN IS A DOCUMENTED APPROXIMATION. The four brain SVGs cannot be tiled fills in Figma (an SVG imports as an editable vector tree, and scaleMode does not apply), so each was rasterized to PNG at 2× natural size with its authored .st0 opacity BAKED INTO THE ALPHA — 0.15/0.2/0.7/0.15 — and tiled at scalingFactor 0.5 to land back at the natural 600px that background-size: auto auto gives it. Rendering brain at full strength was considered and REJECTED: brain-pattern-black.svg, -reversed.svg and -white.svg are the same 37-path drawing with the same #FFFFFF ink and differ ONLY in that declared opacity, so full strength would have made three of the four images identical and reproduced the defect in changes[1]. The rasterized peaks measured 0.149/0.200/0.698/0.149, matching the SVGs' declarations and this contract's independently-measured 0.149 for black/brain.

2026-08-24, changes[2] (d) and (e). (d) community and particle went up as the shipped PNGs unmodified, tiled at their production background-size (1000px / 1400px) rather than normalised — normalising per-pixel alpha would have produced a derived image corresponding to no file in the repo. (e) All 11 tokensUsed entries are now BOUND on the set: solid fill, text, link and border. The border tokens had been bound nowhere in Figma; they are now on a bordered sample rectangle inside each variant, which documents behavior[1] (descendants inherit border-color; the wrapper sets the value) rather than decorating the swatch edge. The doc frames' own strokes had been an unbound #000000 at opacity 0.133 — a hand-typed near-miss of color/border/default's 0.125, and wrong-signed on black.

2026-08-24, changes[2] (f) — NOT YET DONE, the one open item. The 16 doc frames (163:5 … 163:61) are superseded but STILL IN THE FILE. Deleting them was blocked in-session: the Figma MCP's safety classifier refuses a use_figma script that removes pre-existing content, while allowing reads, property mutations, and removal of nodes the script itself created (both probed 2026-08-24). Until a human deletes them this page still has two surfaces that disagree, and the frames are the stale one — they carry the 7-image sharing, the unbound 0.133 strokes and the old labels. Do not resolve the disagreement by editing the frames.
knownIssues: Legacy classes .bg-pattern--brain, -brain-reversed and -brain-black are referenced in 6 UIDS files (mostly ancestor context: _background.scss:47,52; _headline-mixins.scss:103; blockquote.scss; tables.scss; base/_paragraph.scss:174 — stat.scss:182's '&.bg-pattern--brain-reversed' is a SELF-compound, the one exception) plus 7 more in uiowa/uiowa's uids_base (global.scss, layout-builder.scss, cta.scss, forms.scss, main-menu.scss, headings.scss, admin/_claro.scss) — but DEFINED nowhere: no producer exists in uiowa/uiowa code or config. Every layout_builder_styles.style.*.yml `classes:` value ships only the current grammar (bg--{color}--pattern--{type}), verified across all 31 background style configs (16 component + 15 section). They survive only via editor-entered classes in old DB content. Keep as context selectors; never tokenize as color/pattern values — no code path produces them.

DOWNSTREAM: uids_base's two adjacent-section padding-merge lists DISAGREE. global.scss:189-196 uses EXACT selectors (.bg--gold/.bg--black/.bg--gray — no bg--white — plus the three legacy brain names), so current-style combined pattern classes (bg--gold--pattern--particle etc.) never merge there: an exact .bg--gold cannot match the single class token bg--gold--pattern--particle. layout-builder.scss:220-228 instead uses SUBSTRING matchers ([class*="bg--gold"] etc., plus bg--white and the same legacy names), which DO match the combined pattern classes — so merge behavior differs between the two contexts, and the front-end (global.scss) is the one that misses pattern backgrounds. Fix belongs in uiowa/uiowa, not here.

[class*="bg--"] / [class*="bg--gold"] / [class*="--pattern--particle"] substring matching (rather than exact class matching) IS this system's public API — border-color inheritance, link-color overrides, and downstream padding-merge all key off it with no explicit contract otherwise. This is documented and FROZEN, not a bug: renaming any grammar segment (bg--, a color name, or --pattern--) breaks these selectors across 8+ files in two repos — the class grammar (see options) is the thing to treat as the versioned public shape.

The 16 bg--{color}[--pattern--{type}] combos (background.ts allBackgroundOptions) do not each have a unique image: bg--gray--pattern--community and bg--white--pattern--community both use community-pattern--gray.png; bg--white--pattern--brain uses brain-pattern.svg while bg--gray--pattern--brain uses the distinct brain-pattern-white.svg. Full per-combo map (_background-mixins.scss's $backgrounds, $imgpath = '../../assets/images'): black -> brain-pattern-black.svg / community-pattern--black.png / particle-pattern--black.png; gold -> brain-pattern-reversed.svg / community-pattern--white.png / particle-pattern.png; gray -> brain-pattern-white.svg / community-pattern--gray.png / particle-pattern--white.png; white -> brain-pattern.svg / community-pattern--gray.png (shared) / particle-pattern--gold.png. Figma swatches must be drawn from this exact map, not assumed to be 12 distinct images.
